mainTopic: Immodest behavior that costs a wife her כתובה, and a wife found to have vows or blemishes
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier answer. By Torah law a basket on the head (קלתה) is enough, but דת יהודית demands a real covering. רבי זירא asks where רבי יוחנן's rule that a basket avoids פרוע ראש could apply, and אביי (or רב כהנא) answers that it applies when she walks between courtyards through an alleyway. The גמרא then explains more items from the משנה: spinning in the marketplace, talking with every man (with a story from רבה בר בר חנה), cursing the husband's parents, and the קולנית, which it concludes is about behavior and not a physical מום. A new משנה follows: if he betrothed her on condition that she has no נדרים or מומין and she does, there is no קידושין, and if he married her with no condition, she leaves without a כתובה. The גמרא explains why this repeats a משנה in קידושין, then defines the vows as ones of עינוי נפש. רב פפא and רב אשי disagree over which clause that definition explains. Finally, רב and שמואל argue whether she needs a גט when he betrothed her on a condition but married her without one, and אביי's comment continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Torah law allows a basket, Jewish custom does not
steps.stepSummary: The end of the earlier answer: by Torah law a basket on the head is enough, but by דת יהודית even a basket is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: With her basket on her head, it is fine. But by Jewish custom, even her basket is also forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer that started on the previous daf. It splits the head-covering rule into two levels: Torah law and Jewish custom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier question was how an uncovered head can be called only 'custom' (דת יהודית) when it is a Torah rule. The answer is that the Torah requires only a minimal covering, such as a basket (קלתה). Jewish custom requires a real head covering, so a basket alone breaks דת יהודית.

keyTerms.meaning: Her basket, a work basket worn on the head
It is fine, it is acceptable
Jewish custom: standards of modesty that Jewish women accepted on themselves

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a basket does nothing. By Torah law it is enough. It falls short only of the higher standard of דת יהודית.

phrases.english: With her basket on her head, it is fine;
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous daf, which began 'by Torah law.'

phrases.english: but by Jewish custom,
even her basket is also forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַלְתָּהּ שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי, דָּת יְהוּדִית — אֲפִילּוּ קַלְתָּהּ נָמֵי אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer, begun on the previous daf, to the question of how an uncovered head can be only דת יהודית.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the rule into two levels: a Torah minimum and a stricter custom.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An uncovered head is a Torah problem, so it should not be listed under custom.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah requires only a basket-level covering. The custom requires full covering.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A basket satisfies Torah law but not דת יהודית.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: a basket avoids an uncovered head
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי quotes רבי יוחנן: a woman wearing her basket on her head does not break the rule of פרוע ראש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: if she has her basket on her head, there is no problem of an uncovered head.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement is brought: according to רבי יוחנן, wearing a basket is enough to avoid an 'uncovered head.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says the basket is fully enough, with no mention of the higher custom. This sounds like it ignores the rule just taught, that custom forbids a basket alone. That tension sets up רבי זירא's question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It does not involve the problem of

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: קַלְתָּהּ, אֵין בָּהּ מִשּׁוּם פְּרוּעַ רֹאשׁ.
phrases.english: Her basket: there is no problem of an uncovered head.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an אמורא's statement about the same basket case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A basket on the head is not considered an uncovered head.

steps.title: רבי זירא: where could this be true?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks where רבי יוחנן's rule applies. In the marketplace a basket is not enough, and in the courtyard no covering is needed at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא discussed it: Where is this? If you say in the marketplace, that is a violation of Jewish custom! And if instead in the courtyard, then you have not left a single daughter of our father אברהם who can stay married to her husband!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא challenges רבי יוחנן by asking where his rule could apply. Every place he tries seems to fail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the marketplace, the previous step already said a basket is not enough because of דת יהודית. In her own courtyard, if even a basket were required, almost every woman would be breaking the rule and could lose her marriage. Neither place fits, so the rule seems to have no setting.

keyTerms.meaning: He discussed it, he raised a difficulty about it

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira discussed it: Where?
If you say in the marketplace,
that is a matter of Jewish custom!
phrases.notes: He means: in the marketplace a basket alone already breaks Jewish custom, as step 1 said.

phrases.english: And rather, in the courtyard,
if so, you have not left
a daughter of our father Abraham
who stays married to her husband!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָוֵי בַּהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא: הֵיכָא? אִילֵּימָא בְּשׁוּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's statement by testing each possible location.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that a basket is enough
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma: in public a basket is not enough, and in private even a basket would be too strict a demand. So the rule has no possible setting.

steps.title: Answer: walking between courtyards through an alleyway
steps.stepSummary: אביי (some say רב כהנא) answers that רבי יוחנן means a woman walking from one courtyard to another through an alleyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said, and some say it was רב כהנא: it means from courtyard to courtyard, by way of an alleyway.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבי זירא by finding a middle kind of place for רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An alleyway between courtyards is not as private as her own courtyard and not as public as the marketplace. In that middle place, a basket is enough. This saves רבי יוחנן from both sides of the dilemma.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (it was this other rabbi)
Alleyway, a semi-public lane that courtyards open onto

steps.whatToRemember: Head covering works in three levels. In her own courtyard nothing is required. Between courtyards and in an alleyway, a basket is enough. In the marketplace, a full covering is required by דת יהודית.

phrases.english: Abaye said, and some say Rav Kahana said:
From courtyard to courtyard, and by way of an alleyway.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves רבי זירא's dilemma.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines a middle setting that is neither public nor fully private.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every location is either the marketplace or the courtyard, so the rule has no home.
steps.terutzMaskana: A semi-public place exists, and there a basket is enough.

steps.title: Spinning in the marketplace means showing her arms
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's 'spins in the marketplace,' and שמואל explains it as showing her arms to people.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And she spins in the marketplace': רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל, this means she shows her arms to people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to another item in the משנה's list of things that break דת יהודית and explains what is wrong with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spinning itself is ordinary work, so the problem must lie in how she does it. שמואל says that while spinning she uncovers her arms in front of others. That immodesty is the real problem.

phrases.english: And she spins in the marketplace.
phrases.notes: A quote from our משנה's list of things that go against Jewish custom.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
When she shows her arms to people.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְטוֹוֶה בַּשּׁוֹק. אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Spinning in the marketplace' refers to showing her arms.

steps.title: Another view: spinning red thread by her face
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא, quoting אבימי, says the problem is spinning red thread in front of her face.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of אבימי: it means she spins red thread opposite her face.
steps.whatsHappening: A second explanation of 'spinning in the marketplace' is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the problem is not uncovered skin. She holds bright red thread by her face to draw attention to her looks. Both views agree the spinning becomes a way of drawing attention to herself.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said that Avimi said:
When she spins red thread opposite her face.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative to שמואל's explanation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Spinning in the marketplace' refers to spinning red thread by her face.

steps.title: Talking with every man means flirting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'talks with every man' from the משנה, and שמואל explains it as playing around with young men.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And she talks with every man': רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל, this means she jokes and plays around with young men.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next item in the משנה's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simply talking to people is not forbidden. שמואל says the משנה means light, flirting behavior with young men, and that is what breaks דת יהודית.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean a woman may not speak to men. The משנה means flirting behavior.

phrases.english: And she talks with every man.
phrases.notes: Another quote from the משנה's list.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
When she plays around with young men.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְדַבֶּרֶת עִם כׇּל אָדָם. אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Talking with every man' refers to flirting with young men.

steps.title: The story of the Arab woman spinning
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה tells how he and רב עוקבא saw an Arab woman spinning red thread by her face. She threw down her spindle and asked him to hand it back, and רב עוקבא made a comment about her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said: Once I was walking behind רב עוקבא. I saw an Arab woman sitting and casting her spindle, spinning red thread opposite her face. When she saw us, she broke off her spindle and threw it down. She said to me: 'Young man, give me the spindle.' רב עוקבא said something about her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story that shows the behaviors just discussed happening in real life. It ends by setting up a question: what exactly did רב עוקבא say?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her red thread by her face matches אבימי's explanation in step 6. She also threw down her spindle so the young man would talk to her, which looks like 'talking with every man.' Because the story fits both items, the next steps ask which one רב עוקבא meant.

keyTerms.meaning: Her spindle, the tool used for spinning

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said:
One time I was walking
behind Rav Ukva.
I saw a certain Arab woman
who was sitting, casting her spindle,
and spinning red thread opposite her face.
Once she saw us,
she broke off her spindle and threw it down.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרָה לִי: עוּלָם, הַב לִי פֶּלֶךְ.
phrases.english: She said to me: Young man, give me the spindle.
Rav Ukva said a remark about her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה: זִימְנָא חֲדָא הֲוָה קָאָזֵילְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the behaviors from steps 6 and 7 happening in a real case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A real example of a woman spinning red thread by her face and starting a conversation with a stranger.

steps.title: What did רב עוקבא say?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which item from the משנה רב עוקבא was pointing to.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did he say about her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question. It sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story fits two items in the משנה, spinning and talking. The גמרא wants to know which one רב עוקבא named.

phrases.english: What did he say about her?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the remark mentioned at the end of the story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which item in the משנה רב עוקבא applied to the woman.

steps.title: Two answers: spinning or talking
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says רב עוקבא called her one who 'spins in the marketplace.' The רבנן say he called her one who 'talks with every man.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: he said about her 'spins in the marketplace.' The רבנן said: he said about her 'talks with every man.'
steps.whatsHappening: Two opinions answer the question, each linking the woman to a different item in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא focuses on her red thread by her face, which fits אבימי's explanation of spinning. The רבנן focus on how she drew the young man into talking with her. Both treat her behavior as the kind of immodesty the משנה lists.
steps.whatToRemember: The items in the משנה are about drawing attention in an immodest way. That can mean showing skin, highlighting her beauty, or flirting.

phrases.english: Ravina said: He said about her, 'she spins in the marketplace.'
The Rabbis said:
He said about her, 'she talks with every man.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבינא says 'spinning in the marketplace.' The רבנן say 'talking with every man.'

steps.title: Cursing the husband's parents in front of his children
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes אבא שאול from the משנה, and שמואל adds that cursing his parents in front of his children also counts. He gives a פסוק as a memory sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול says: also a woman who curses her husband's parents in front of him. רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: even if she curses his parents in front of his children. The memory sign is: 'אפרים and מנשה will be to me like ראובן and שמעון.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes אבא שאול's case from the משנה, and שמואל stretches it to cover cursing the husband's parents in front of the husband's children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'in his presence.' שמואל says that cursing in front of his children is just as bad. The פסוק shows that grandchildren are treated like children: יעקב says his grandsons אפרים and מנשה are like his own sons ראובן and שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: his parents (literally, those who gave birth to him)
his children (literally, those he gave birth to)

phrases.english: Abba Shaul says:
Also a woman who curses his parents in his presence.
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
When she curses his parents in front of his children.
And your memory sign is:
"Ephraim and Menashe, like Reuven
and Shimon, they shall be mine."

steps.triggerLanguage: אבא שאול אומר: אף המקללת יולדיו בפניו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next opinion in the משנה after the discussion of the red-thread story
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cursing the husband's parents in front of his children is like cursing them in front of him

steps.title: An example of such a curse
steps.stepSummary: רבה gives an example of the kind of curse meant: 'May a lion eat the old man in front of his son!'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: for example, she said to him, 'May a lion eat the old man in front of his son!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives a real-life example of the curse the משנה is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds no new rule. It shows how the case looks in practice: a harsh curse against the husband's father, said in front of family.

phrases.english: Rabba said: For example, that she said to him,
"May a lion eat the old man
in front of his son!"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a concrete example of the case explained in step 11
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A curse like 'May a lion eat the grandfather' is the kind of curse meant

steps.title: What is a קולנית?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי טרפון's addition of a קולנית and asks what that word means.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון says: also a loud woman. What is a 'loud woman'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last opinion in the משנה and asks for the meaning of the word קולנית. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word only says 'loud.' The גמרא wants to know exactly what kind of loudness is serious enough to lose her כתובה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon says:
Also a loud woman.
What is a "loud woman"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next opinion in the משנה

steps.title: שמואל: she raises her voice about intimate matters
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that a קולנית is a woman who loudly argues about matters of intimacy, so others hear.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: she raises her voice about matters of intimacy.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers: a קולנית is a woman who loudly fights with her husband about intimacy, so others can hear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This puts קולנית under immodest behavior, the topic of this משנה. The problem is her conduct, which embarrasses her husband.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
When she raises her voice
about matters of intimacy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב יהודה אמר שמואל: במשמעת קולה על עסקי תשמיש
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קולנית loudly quarrels about intimate matters

steps.title: A ברייתא: her voice is heard in another courtyard
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives a different definition: during intimacy her voice can be heard in the next courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: when she is intimate in this courtyard, and her voice is heard in another courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a second definition of קולנית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the loudness comes from the intimacy itself, not from arguing. That sounds more like a physical problem than bad behavior, which is what the next step will attack.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
When she is intimate in this courtyard
and her voice is heard in another courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to step 13, different from שמואל's
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קולנית is one whose voice is heard in another courtyard during intimacy

steps.title: Then it belongs with the physical blemishes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: if that's the meaning, the case should be listed with the מומים, not here.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then let it be taught together with the blemishes in the משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא's definition. Loudness during intimacy is a physical issue, so it should be listed with the מומים later in the פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה lists bad behavior, not body problems. The מומים have their own משנה at the end of the פרק. Since קולנית appears here, it must be about behavior.

phrases.english: But then let it be taught together with the blemishes
in the mishna!
phrases.notes: He means the later משנה in this פרק that lists physical blemishes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא's definition in step 15
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A loud voice during intimacy is a physical מום, so it would be listed with the מומים, not in a משנה about behavior

steps.title: Back to the first explanation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the first explanation, שמואל's, is the correct one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear as we answered at first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the ברייתא's reading and goes back to שמואל's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the case is in a משנה about behavior, קולנית must mean loud, immodest quarreling about intimacy, as שמואל said.
steps.whatToRemember: A קולנית loses her כתובה because of immodest behavior. She is someone who loudly argues about intimate matters, not someone with a physical problem.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear
as we answered at first.
phrases.notes: This points back to שמואל's explanation in step 14.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge in step 16 and returns to step 14
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: קולנית means a woman who loudly quarrels about intimate matters, as שמואל said

steps.title: New משנה: marrying a woman who turns out to have vows
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules on a woman who turns out to have נדרים. If he made a condition, there is no קידושין. If he married her without a condition, she leaves without a כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a man betroths a woman on condition that she has no vows, and it turns out she has vows, she is not betrothed. If he married her without saying anything and it turns out she has vows, she leaves without a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins about a wife who turns out to have נדרים. It gives two different results depending on whether he made a condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a clear condition, the condition was broken, so the קידושין never took effect. Without a condition, the marriage is valid, but she hid a problem from him, so she can be divorced without a כתובה.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two endings. With a condition, there was never any marriage. Without a condition, she is truly married and needs a גט, she just loses her כתובה.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who betroths a woman
on condition that she has no vows on her,
and it turns out she has vows on her:
she is not betrothed.
If he married her without specifying,
and it turns out she has vows on her:
she leaves without a marriage contract.

steps.triggerLanguage: מתני׳ המקדש את האשה על מנת שאין עליה נדרים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of the previous one ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A condition that she has no נדרים cancels the קידושין if it is broken. Without a condition, she is married but leaves without a כתובה.

steps.title: The משנה's ruling on a wife found to have blemishes
steps.stepSummary: With a condition of no מומין, there is no קידושין. Without a condition, she leaves without a כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he betrothed her on condition that she has no blemishes, and blemishes were found on her, she is not betrothed. If he married her without saying anything, and blemishes were found, she leaves without a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the same two-part rule it gave for נדרים to a woman who turns out to have physical מומין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An open condition makes the קידושין fail completely when it is not met. Without a condition, the marriage is valid. But because he never would have agreed to marry a woman with such a flaw, she loses her כתובה money.

keyTerms.meaning: He married her without stating any condition
She leaves the marriage without receiving her כתובה

phrases.english: On condition that she has no blemishes
and blemishes were found on her
she is not betrothed.
If he married her without specifying
and blemishes were found on her
she leaves without a marriage contract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same two-part rule from the נדרים case to physical blemishes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A condition that is not met cancels the קידושין. Without a condition, she is divorced without a כתובה.

steps.title: Which blemishes count for women
steps.stepSummary: Any מום that disqualifies a כהן from service also counts as a מום for a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the blemishes that disqualify כהנים also disqualify women.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה defines what counts as a מום by pointing to the known list of מומין that disqualify כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not make a new list. It borrows the list already used for כהנים, so the same physical defects apply here.

phrases.english: All the blemishes that disqualify priests
disqualify women.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the term מומין used in the previous ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מומין of כהנים are the standard for women.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives a two-part rule. A condition that is not met means no קידושין. No condition means she leaves without a כתובה. The מומין are the ones that disqualify כהנים.

steps.title: Why repeat what we already learned in קידושין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that an almost identical משנה appears in מסכת קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: But we also learned a משנה just like this about קידושין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה for repeating a rule that already appears in מסכת קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה is not supposed to repeat itself for no reason. If the same rule already appears in קידושין, why teach it here again?

keyTerms.meaning: And we also learned (in another משנה)

phrases.english: Gemara: And we also learned
concerning betrothal, a case just like this!
phrases.notes: This refers to the משנה in קידושין 50a, which teaches almost the same thing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְנַן נָמֵי גַּבֵּי קִדּוּשִׁין כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by questioning why the משנה repeats itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The repetition of the משנה in both כתובות and קידושין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rule that is already taught should not need to be taught again.

steps.title: Each tractate needed its own half
steps.stepSummary: Here the main point is the כתובה, and the קידושין part came along with it. In קידושין it is the opposite.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, the כתובה rule was needed, and the קידושין rule was taught along with it. There, the קידושין rule was needed, and the כתובה rule was taught along with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that each משנה was taught for the topic of its own מסכת. The other half of the rule just came along with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two-part rule is taught as one unit. In כתובות, the needed half is losing the כתובה. In קידושין, the needed half is that the קידושין is cancelled. So neither one is really a wasted repeat.

phrases.english: Here, he needed the law of marriage contracts,
so he taught betrothal because of marriage contracts.
There, he needed the law of betrothal,
so he taught marriage contracts because of betrothal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא about the repetition.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each source has its own main purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה here is a pointless repeat of the one in קידושין.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each מסכת teaches the half that fits its own topic, and the other half comes along with it.

steps.title: Which vows the משנה means
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק, says the נדרים in the משנה are vows not to eat meat, not to drink wine, or not to wear colored clothes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק: these are the vows they meant. That she will not eat meat, that she will not drink wine, and that she will not dress up in colored clothes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the נדרים case of the משנה and defines which kinds of vows count as a hidden flaw.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every small vow counts. These examples are vows that make her life harder, and a husband would reasonably object to them.

keyTerms.meaning: These are the vows they spoke about

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak:
These are the vows they spoke about:
phrases.notes: He means the vows mentioned in the משנה from step 18.

phrases.english: that she will not eat meat,
and that she will not drink wine,
and that she will not adorn herself with colored garments.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק בְּאֵלּוּ נְדָרִים אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the נדרים case of the משנה to define it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The vows in the משנה are vows that involve self-denial: meat, wine, and colored clothing.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same list and calls these vows matters of עינוי נפש.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught in a ברייתא: these are the vows they meant, things that involve self-affliction. That she will not eat meat, will not drink wine, and will not dress up in colored clothes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רבי יוחנן, to support him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא adds the general category, עינוי נפש, which explains why these examples were chosen. They are vows that make her suffer.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (in a ברייתא)

phrases.english: It was also taught so in a baraita:
These are the vows they spoke about:
matters that involve self-affliction:
that she will not eat meat,
and that she will not drink wine,
and that she will not adorn herself with colored garments.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's definition with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's definition of the vows
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same list, labeled עינוי נפש

steps.title: רב פפא asks which clause this explains
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks which part of the משנה the definition of vows refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא discussed it: which part of the משנה is this about?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא opens a question: does this definition go on the first part of the משנה, where he made a condition, or the second part, where he did not? This sets up the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה has two cases, and a definition of vows might fit only one of them. רב פפא will check each option.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa discussed it:
To which clause does this refer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks where in the משנה the definition from steps 23 and 24 belongs.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the list of vows explains the רישא or the סיפא of the משנה

steps.title: It cannot be the first clause
steps.stepSummary: If he made a condition about vows, he clearly cares, so any vow at all should break the condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is about the first part: since he is particular, even any vow at all should count!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא rejects the idea that the list of vows explains the first case, where he made a condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making a condition shows he cares about vows of any kind. So any vow, even a small one, means the condition was not met, and there is no reason to limit it to vows of עינוי נפש.

phrases.english: If we say it refers to the first clause:
phrases.notes: The first clause is where he betrothed her on condition that she has no vows.

phrases.english: since he is particular,
then even vows about any matter should also count!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first option and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The option that the definition goes on the רישא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An open condition covers every vow, so a limited list makes no sense there.

steps.title: It refers to the second clause
steps.stepSummary: The list of vows explains the case where he married her without a condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is about the second part.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא concludes that the definition goes on the case where he married her without a condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a condition, we only assume he would object to serious vows. So only vows of עינוי נפש let him divorce her without a כתובה.

phrases.english: Rather, it refers to the latter clause.
phrases.notes: The latter clause is where he married her without a condition, and she leaves without a כתובה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the רישא, settles on the סיפא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In רב פפא's view, vows of עינוי נפש are the vows that matter when he married her without a condition. With a condition, any vow counts. רב אשי disagrees in the next step.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב פפא: with a condition, any vow cancels the קידושין. Without a condition, only vows of עינוי נפש (meat, wine, colored clothes) let him divorce her without a כתובה. The next step brings רב אשי, who disagrees.

steps.title: רב אשי: The list of vows explains the case with a condition
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the list of vows explains the first case of the משנה, where he made a condition. A man's insistence only counts for vows that people normally care about.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The list really refers to the first case, where he made a condition. If it is something people usually care about, his insistence counts. If it is something people usually don't care about, his insistence doesn't count.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different answer to רב פפא's question. He says the list of vows does belong to the case where the man made a condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 26 argued that a man who makes a condition clearly cares about any vow at all. רב אשי disagrees: a general condition only covers what normal people care about. So only vows of עינוי נפש, like not eating meat, break the condition; small vows don't.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, in truth (used to bring back an idea that seemed rejected)
The first clause of the משנה
They are particular, they care about it

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with step 27. There the list explained the case with no condition. רב אשי says it explains the case with a condition, because normal standards limit what the condition covers.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Actually, it refers to the first clause,
phrases.notes: The first clause is the case where he betrothed her on condition that she has no vows.

phrases.english: and a matter that people are particular about —
his insistence counts as insistence.
A matter that people are not particular about —
his insistence does not count as insistence.
phrases.notes: So a small vow doesn't break his condition, and the קידושין stay valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to רב פפא's question. It goes against step 27 and pushes back on the reasoning of step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the condition by normal human standards
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A man who makes a condition about vows cares about every vow, so the list could not refer to that case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even with a condition, only vows people normally care about break it, so the list fits the first clause.
steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי: a condition only covers what people normally care about, so the list of vows of עינוי נפש can explain the case where he made a condition.

steps.title: רב and שמואל argue: conditional betrothal, then marriage with no condition
steps.stepSummary: If a man made קידושין on a condition and then married her without saying any condition, and the condition was not met, רב says she needs a גט and שמואל says she does not. אביי begins to comment.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: If he betrothed her on a condition and married her without stating a condition, רב says she needs a גט from him, and שמואל says she does not need a גט from him. אביי said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: a מחלוקת between רב and שמואל. At the end, the גמרא sets up אביי's comment, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether the later נישואין with no condition shows that the man let go of his original condition. רב says she needs a גט, so the marriage may be real. שמואל says she needs no גט, so the original condition still stands and the marriage never took hold.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (opens a disagreement between אמוראים)
He betrothed her on a condition
He married her without stating anything

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic question for the rest of the sugya: does a condition from the קידושין carry over into the נישואין when nobody repeats it?

phrases.english: It was stated:
If he betrothed her on a condition
and married her without specifying,
phrases.notes: The case is that the condition later turned out not to be fulfilled.

phrases.english: Rav said: She requires a bill of divorce from him.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה הֵימֶנּוּ גֵּט.
phrases.english: And Shmuel said: She does not require a bill of divorce from him.
Abaye said:
phrases.notes: What אביי actually says comes on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: קִידְּשָׁה עַל תְּנַאי וּכְנָסָהּ סְתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic connected to the משנה's cases of conditional marriage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: she needs a גט. שמואל: she does not need a גט.
